newsitem.title: CHINA: China makes rules on brokers trading forex shares.
newsitem.headline: China makes rules on brokers trading forex shares.

text.p: China on Tuesday issued a set of rules to govern domestic and foreign brokerages trading the nation's foreign currency shares listed at home and abroad.
The rules come into effect on December 1.

The rules, published in the Shanghai Securities News, defined domestic brokerages as securities houses and trust and investment companies each with a minimum 50 million yuan in net assets or capital devoted solely to securities.

Foreign brokerages must be investment banks, securities houses or other financial organisations allowed to do securities business in accordance with laws and rules in their mother countries, the rules said. They must have an equivalent of 50 million yuan in net assets or securities capital.

The shares covered included B shares listed in the Shanghai and Shenzhen stock exchanges, H shares listed in Hong Kong and other Chinese foreign currency shares listed in New York, Singapore and Australia, the rules said.

The rules also said that a brokerage must have at least 80 million yuan or equivalent to underwrite a company's share issue and at least 120 million yuan or equivalent to be lead underwriter or chief international coordinator.
Other conditions for brokerages include that they must have appropriate offices, a minimum of specialised personnel and a record of no illegal behaviour for at least two years.
